title: Gujarat's Swaminarayan
hook: a boy with a staff and a loincloth walks out of his village and keeps walking until he reaches Gujarat

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa ended on the hill at Sabarimala, where every pilgrim is called swami. This week gave us a king welcomed home with flowers, and a boy who rode home on a tigress. Which one walked with you? Day one thousand four hundred.

Bare feet on a mountain path, high in the Himalayas. A boy, thin from fasting, wearing only a loincloth, carrying a staff, a string of beads and a small bundle. No family with him. No guide. In the stories his followers tell, he left home young, and he's been walking ever since: through snow, through forests, across rivers, from one holy place to the next, looking for something. People along the road call him Nilkanth. Today, the start of a new region, Gujarat, and the walk that brought this boy there.
screen: `BARE FEET IN THE HIMALAYAS` → `A BOY WITH A STAFF` → `NILKANTH, WALKING`

segments.voice: First, the boy. Tradition says he was born Ghanshyam, in a village called Chhapaiya, not far from Ayodhya in the north. His family were devout, and he was a child who loved scripture and prayer. After his parents died, he left home as a young renunciant, a brahmachari, and took the name Nilkanth, blue-throat, one of the names of Shiva. Second, the walk. His followers tell it as a long journey on foot across India: the Himalayas, the holy sites of the east, the temples of the south. Tradition tells of him standing in hard austerities in the mountains, of meeting yogis and teachers, and of moving on from each one. He wasn't wandering for its own sake. He was asking questions and not settling for half answers. Third, the arrival. At last he comes west, into Gujarat, to a small ashram at a village called Loj. It belongs to a teacher named Ramanand Swami, and one of his disciples, Muktanand, is there to receive the young stranger. Nilkanth asks his questions: about the soul, about God, about the world and what binds us to it. And this time he stays. That's the seed of what's now called the Swaminarayan tradition, a living Hindu community with deep roots in Gujarat and temples well beyond it. Tomorrow, what happened at Loj and the name that came after. For now, notice the shape. A tradition that today feels rooted, organized and very much at home, began with a boy who had no home at all, only a road and a question. What question are you still walking with?
screen: `GHANSHYAM BECOMES NILKANTH` · `A WALK ACROSS INDIA` · `ARRIVING AT LOJ IN GUJARAT` · `A BOY WITH A ROAD AND A QUESTION`

segments.voice: Walk with a question. Sit tall, as if you had a staff in your hand. Breathe in, and let a real question come up, one you haven't finished with: about God, about yourself, about what matters. Don't answer it. Just let it walk with you, breath after breath, the way Nilkanth carried his questions from place to place. When the mind wanders, come back to the question and to the breath. If you pray, you can hold the question as a prayer. The bell holds the time.
Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, Nilkanth: the boy born Ghanshyam, who walked across India with his questions until he reached Ramanand Swami's ashram at Loj. Today's word.
Your line: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, carry your one big question with you on a walk, even a short one, and let your feet do some of the asking. Day one thousand four hundred.
